subject: Setting timezone for breaks and labels

messages.author: 9e8f9b870a2e6cdf
messages.subject: Setting timezone for breaks and labels
parts:
Hi,

I have a some data that consists of pairs of timestamps and values.
The timestamps are recorded in the timezone GMT. 
Recording starts at 00:00 GMT and last for 3 days.

My own timezone is CEST.

I would like to make scatter plot of this, but show the data as it would appear in the original timezone (GMT).
I tried this with adding a

   scale_x_datetime( tz="GMT")

However the data appeared as it had been shifted by about 2 hours.
The graphs shows days on the major break lines. The data starts about 2 hours from the first major break line.

A complete example is:

start <- ISOdate(2001, 10, 10, 0, tz = "GMT")
d <- data.frame(
        tms   = c( start, start + round(runif(20, max = 3 * 86400) ) ),
        val   = runif(21) )

p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=tms,y=val)) +
     geom_point() +
     scale_x_datetime( tz="GMT")

After some experimenting I found that the major breaks are displayed in my timezone,
while the data is displayed in the GMT timezone.

This can be seen with:
     scale_x_datetime( format = "%d/%b %H:%M", tz="GMT")
It shows that the first break is on:
    09 Oct 22:00 hours

Is there are way to also have the breaks and labels on the x-axis to be shown in the GMT time zone?


Have fun,
Frans.

Hi Frans, 

It was fun, especially cause I dont get the error you're talking about! :)

I plotted this 
p <- ggplot(d[1:3,], aes(x=tms,y=val)) +
+      geom_point() +
+      scale_x_datetime( format = "%d/%b %H:%M", tz="GMT", major='hour')

just for added clarity and the first point is on 0:00, Oct 10. That's what you want, right? So i dont have to fix anything.

I believe I'm fully upto date with R and ggplot, that's the only thing I can thnk of
